## Homepage section order

Based on search results and press materials, inferred structure:

1. Hero section with tagline "Train and Run AI on the Right Data"
2. Value proposition: Data readiness as the physical AI bottleneck
3. Platform capabilities overview (Annotate, Active, Index sections)
4. Video/media demonstration section
5. Customer logos and social proof
6. Case study highlights (Standard AI, Woven by Toyota)
7. Pricing tiers comparison
8. Call-to-action for demo or product exploration
9. FAQ or resources section
10. Footer with links to solutions, customers, pricing, resources

## Proof placement

Petabyte scale: Announced in Series C funding press release, February 2026. Stat: "5 petabytes exceeds GPT-4 training data by 3x."

10x revenue growth from physical AI customers: Series C press release, stated as "revenue from physical AI customers grew tenfold" in past 12 months.

300+ customer teams: Mentioned in funding announcement and multiple marketing materials.

Named customers (Woven by Toyota, AXA, UiPath, Zipline): Listed in funding press release.

Standard AI case study: Dedicated case study page at encord.com/customers/standard-ai/, claims "60-80% reduction in labeling costs."

Enterprise compliance: SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR mentioned in search results. No dedicated compliance page found in navigation.

## Claim qualification

"AI-native data infrastructure" - Used as descriptive positioning term in funding materials and product pages. No definition of what "AI-native" means provided on pages accessed.

"The data layer for physical AI" - Framing claim. Positions Encord as foundational infrastructure layer, not point solution.

"Closed loop" approach - Claimed to connect "data, human reviewers, and models in a single platform." Differentiation claim vs. point tools.

"Data readiness" bottleneck - CEO statement quoted in press materials. Reframes physical AI problem space away from compute/model size.

"Model-assisted labeling" - Feature claim with integration to SAM 2 and GPT-4o mentioned.

## Type and color

No specific font name or color hex values could be extracted via WebFetch due to JavaScript rendering. Search results suggest use of modern, sans-serif typography (inferred from industry standards for B2B SaaS platforms). Dark theme support status unknown due to page access limitations.

## Conversion path

Primary CTA structure: "Explore product" and "Book demo" buttons placed in navigation and likely repeated on hero section.

Secondary conversion: Blog content and comparison pages (vs. Roboflow, SuperAnnotate, etc.) appear designed to capture search traffic and lead to demo requests.

Tertiary conversion: Case studies (Standard AI page) provide social proof and specific ROI metrics (60-80% cost reduction claim) before conversion ask.

Qualification path appears to route toward "Book demo" rather than free trial signup. No free tier mentioned in pricing search results.

## Distinctive

Closed-loop integration: Encord ties data curation, annotation, and model evaluation into a single traceable workflow, not offering these as separate modules. This is positioned as differentiation vs. best-of-breed point solutions. Every press release emphasizes this integration rather than individual feature depth.

## Noise

Alternatives/comparison page strategy: Encord has dedicated comparison pages vs. Roboflow, SuperAnnotate, V7, Label Studio, Labelbox, Supervisely, CVAT. This is category-standard competitive positioning but represents 6-8 pages with similar structure and messaging across the site. Common pattern in B2B SaaS but creates content repetition.
